annotations.title: Find what the archive says about a passage

description: Compare a passage of text (an article, a headline, a draft, a question) with the whole archive and return what The Durability Curve has already published on it, grouped: essays, ledger claims, weekly calls, laws, free tools and AI models. Each result carries its URL and a share: how much of the passage's distinctive vocabulary it uses. possible_repeat is true when an essay (with its best ledger rows) shares at least 45% of that vocabulary: on the live archive it flagged 13 of 21 paragraphs taken from essays and none of 4 unrelated passages. It is a word-overlap signal, not a judgement: whether a topic is covered is in the essay itself. These tools retrieve The Durability Curve's public material. They do not certify that any claim is true.

per_kind.description: How many results of each kind, 1 to 10. Defaults: 5 essays, 5 claims, 3 calls, 2 laws, 2 tools, 3 models.

text.description: The passage, headline, question or topic to compare with the archive, as text. Paste the words themselves: this tool does not open links.
